the discriminative power of convolutional activations can be enhanced by transforming the activations in a new space that is more discriminative than the original one, and that the new space can be defined by a data-dependent linear transformation of the original space.

a) the discriminative aspects in the target data set are more important than the spatial structure of the convolutional features; and b) the general object categories present in the target data sets can be used to transform the structured features to a highly discriminative representation.

(i) the spatial structure of the convolutional features is not of much help in the presence large variations in scene layout; and (ii) a discriminative representation of the convolutional activations in a new feature space that incorporates the general object categories present in indoor scenes leads to a significant improvement in scene classification performance.
